notes: Read all five units, all seven candidates and the review. Anchored the seventeen-to-one allegation to the statement's contemporary COVID-19 relief bill, resolved the opposed corporate giveaway and desired worker-oriented response, and identified workers as the intended beneficiaries of the Five Principles. Restored the excessive-frequency assessment of prior bailouts, swift coordinated action with class-oriented organizations, and the source's characterization of capitalist bosses and allied politicians.

claims.claim_text: DSA says the U.S. government has too often bailed out corporations and banks rather than working people.

At the statement's publication during COVID-19, Democrats and Republicans were said to back a relief bill allocating seventeen times more financial relief to big business than direct assistance to workers.
Workers should unite against that business-heavy COVID-19 relief allocation and support a response prioritizing people rather than profit.
During the crisis, workers should act quickly and jointly with organizations fighting for working-class needs.
The statement characterizes the ruling class as capitalist bosses and Democratic and Republican politicians beholden to them.
The Five Principles of Just COVID-19 Relief and Stimulus are characterized as a first step toward substantive gains for the working class.
